reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs and minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are spawning from the bank to 5 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in grass 5-12 feet of water with Texas rigged worms, wacky rig senko and chatterbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good using lizards, creature baits, and shallow crankbaits on beds in the backs of coves, cuts, and big shallow flats.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good stacked up in the reeds hitting Texas rigs or any small profile green bait. Bass are moving to the hydrilla late in the evenings and early morning to feed.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs to them by dropping to bottom and reeling smoothly and continuously for about five cranks.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Prespawn crappie are being caught in the creeks.
reports.by: Jeffery Sojourner, Sojourner Fishing LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are spawning in wind-protected shallow pockets in 4-6 feet of water. Look for small male bass around sandy banks in mouths of coves. Small streamers and craw patterns should produce bass. Crappie and catfish should be moving shallow when the weather stabilizes, wooly buggers should work well.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good behind timber lines in flats and old roadways. Bass are shallow hitting wacky senkos and flukes around bushes in spawning flats and pond dams in the 2-5 feet, or Texas rigged creature baits in 2-4 feet around big timber and some bushes. Crappie are excellent from the mouth of coves to the back of coves with natural colored jigs. Even more crappie are spawning in the timber west of the bridge. Look for crappie to be in all stages of the spawn within the next two weeks.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the weeds on plastics.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are very close to the spawn. A slab or a lipless crankbait should put them in the boat. Black bass are in the late stages of the prespawn, so a jerkbait or slow rolled spinnerbait are good bait choices.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 7.86 pounds are fair off the rocks on Hag’s Hurricanes and glide baits and around the flats. and staging areas on squarebill crankbaits and spinnerbaits in 2-8 feet. Crappie are fair to 11 inches on jigs in 8-12 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 2-15 feet with chartreuse jigs. Crappie pattern is consistent with fish in all stages of the spawn. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Largemouth bass are good on rocks and brush piles with watermelon candy brush hogs, buzz baits and spinnerbaits. Crappie are good on brush 12-17 feet with minnows.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Numbers of bass can be caught around the trees with swimbaits, swim jigs, chatterbaits or with slow presentation flukes or wacky style senkos.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair around weed lines on plastics.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in all stages of the spawn. As the water temperature increases the bass will become more aggressive. Bass are spawning in 2-5 feet of water on the inside of grass hitting a buzz bait or wacky worm senko.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing Tour

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: To target these fish, use 1/2 ounce to 1-1/2 ounce slabs and spinnerbaits. The crappie bite is strong around docks, bridges, and in creeks, with minnows or jigs proving to be effective.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 10 feet of water hitting creature baits. Crappie are in 15-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in all stages of the spawn hitting creature baits and soft plastics. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting soft plastic lizards and craw worms in 2-7 feet of water on reeds and stumps.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass action continues to be good near spawning beds on soft plastics worms and centipedes.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been good with some very nice fish being landed still full of eggs. Crappie are fair to good in the shallows to 21 feet around structure or timber using jigs.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, with Bradley Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent from 6 inches to 12 feet of water. Crappie jigs are out producing minnows and hand ties.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass are spawning in wind-protected shallow pockets in 4-6 feet of water. Crappie are excellent from 10 inches to 20 feet of water. Crappie jigs are out producing minnows and hand ties.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to good in boat slips and on brush on jigs and shallow on jigs.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are still on the bank spawning, with some big females still prespawn. A few bass are starting to migrate into deeper water.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are pulling up shallow. Smaller male black bass are moving to the shallows on warm windy banks. The crappie should be moving shallowly in 60-65-degree water. Lake Fork crappie fishing has been steady with numbers of big fish possible when the winds allow. Good numbers of crappie on timber in 6-20 feet close to spawning areas. Wind directions and wind speeds are dictating a lot of the crappie’s location and demeanor.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in all stages of the spawn hitting creature baits and soft plastics. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water feeding on shad. Crappie are moving into the creeks and pockets getting ready to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie limits are possible on small minnows or jigs fished near structures, creek entrances and in the back of the creeks. Many of the sand bass are still spawning on the upper ends near Tin Top, however many are returning to the main lake and can be caught in numbers on white and chartreuse slabs near humps and ridges. Largemouth bass are also moving into the shallows to their spawning beds. Largemouth bass anglers are reporting some good catches on soft plastics and spinner baits working sloughs and docks.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on spinnerbaits and worms fished around heavy cover both up river and in Willis Creek. Crappie are fair in shallow water spawning areas and up river suspended on stumps.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Massive school of white bass are good on the edges of humps in 22-25 feet of water with �¾-1 ounce slabs with a stinger hook.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Greenbelt fishing report
reports.text: Reports of anglers targeting crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are really starting to pattern up in the shallows eating chatterbaits, frogs and spinnerbaits. Crappie are decent in Luces Bayou eating small jigs very close to brush piles.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in all stages of the spawn hitting creature baits and soft plastics. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on soft plastics, swimbaits and swim jigs from the bank to 12 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Some big bass to 9.85 pounds are possible. Bass are spawning in the shallows hitting your favorite soft plastic bait. Crappie are in the shallow timber in the creek.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass are spawning in wind-protected shallow pockets in 4-6 feet of water.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 10-15 feet of water on brush with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Many bass are on or around beds with this first wave of spawn. Bass are on beds fishing wacky senkos under and near docks, or in shallow grass with your favorite plastics.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair in or near to river channels and on points in 20-45 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 2-30 feet of water on brush piles, submerged timber, and submerged cover close to a drop off ledge. Largemouth bass are staging around spawning pockets in 4-10 feet of water. Crappie are still on deep brush and trees in 20 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass and crappie can be caught in spawning areas and backs of creeks. Crappie are in 3 feet or less hitting minnows. Largemouth bass are in 4 feet or less on Texas rig and chatterbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on chatterbaits, swimbaits and Texas rigged junebug worms fishing in the hydrilla. Crappie are good using minnows and power bait champ minnows on �¼ ounce mushroom jig heads in 15-20 feet on brush piles. Sand bass are good in the discharge area using slab spoons and underspin jigs.
reports.by: Hambone guide service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with chartreuse jigs and rosie red minnows. Walleye are good in the evening hours and early mornings in many areas of the lake with imitation shad, slab spoons, minnows, bottom bouncers, floating worm harnesses and pearl blue plastics are great.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millers Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Catfish are good and the crappie bite is improving.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on topwater frogs or weightless senko. Crappie are fair on a white or chartreuse crappie jig on brush piles.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: The majority of bass were caught in the shallow creek areas. Female bass are starting to parade just outside the spawning grounds. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent with shallow Carolina rigs, or shallow paddle tail swimbaits. Crappie are fair with chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water. The spawn is starting and bass are beginning to flood the shallows as the water temperature creeps into the 60s. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Focus on holes in the reed banks where bass will set up on their beds. Crappie were fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on minnows and jigs roaming throughout the lake. Largemouth bass and white bass are slow with few reports.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting in the brush 2-4 feet of water on spinnerbaits, chatterbaits, and green pumpkin creature baits Texas rigged. Main Lake bass are moving up shallow to 2-12 feet of water off points with hard bottoms and brush. White bass are moving shallow in the same areas as black bass. Some crappie reported up to The Colorado River on shallow rock bluffs.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass bite is improving and fish are moving shallow to spawn.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good spawning along the bank, or staged in 8-16 feet of water. Bass are good spawning along the bank, with some staging to spawn or post spawn in less than 8 feet of water on boat houses at the ends of docks hitting spinnerbaits, chatterbait and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow, but now that the lake is settling the crappie spawn is around the corner.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in 2-5 feet of water on swim jigs or bladed jig around grass lines. Crappie fair on a white crappie jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Lake Raven bass fishing is heating up! The bass are working the shallows with 10-12 inch worms along the edge of the hydrilla and water lines. Chatterbaits, dropshots, and wacky rigs are a good set of bait options for anglers seeking to join in on the bass fishing. No reports of crappie or catfish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Look for big bait balls in 25-34 feet of water with 3/4 ounce slabs with 2 jigs tied above working best spread at least 16 inches apart. White bass are also still being caught in the feeder creeks above the lake with small roadrunner type baits and small crappie jigs. Crappie are fair and numbers are showing up in the creeks and shallow water with minnows.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are in 3-6 feet of water in isolated bois d’arc trees, or rip rap near the dam.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass and small hybrids are scattered in 25-30 feet of water on points with slabs and jigs. Reports of Crappie being caught on minnows in shallow water on both the Richland and Chambers Creek tributaries.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: The Black bass bite is still fair.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on minnows and jigs off the bottom near docks and on concrete structure. Bass are fair on crankbaits and spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: After the sun has risen and been up for around 40 minutes, look at the 30-34 feet edges of slow tapering areas for sluggish fish, presenting white or chrome, 3/4 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs by dropping to bottom and reeling smoothly and continuously for about five cranks. Largemouth bass continue to move shallower with the spring warm-up.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite continues to improve in shallow and mid depths. Largemouth bass bite has improved. On warmer days bass are good on rip-rap with squarebill crankbaits, senkos and spinnerbaits in 4-12 feet.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Suspended bass are in marinas near docks and in the backs of pockets. Crappie can be caught near creeks and coves on brush and structure.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with many fish in 1-8 feet of water on lizards, brush hogs, Texas rigs, Carolina rigs, senkos and wacky worms. Bass are good with frogs in the flooded bushes. Crappie bite is improving daily in 3-6 feet on jigs.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Post spawn bass are feeding in open water hitting spinnerbaits, swimbaits and topwater. Big bass can be caught on bluff walls on the main lake working towards cove entrances with creature baits. Bass are good using lizards, creature baits, and shallow crankbaits on beds in the backs of coves, cuts, and big shallow flats.
reports.by: Randal Frisbie, Central Texas Fishing Guide, LLC

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in the middle of creek and river channels.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on minnows but good on jigs. Bass are in 5-6 feet of water and in 12 feet of water. Bass are good with crankbaits. A lunker 13.2 pound bass was caught.. Good bass caught all the way up the submerged grass on the edge of the water but are not quite on beds yet. The crappie bite is good in 15 feet of water in the creek channels all the way into the grass depending on which area of the lake you are fishing. Minnows on slip floats are outperforming jigs for crappie.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Male crappie are bedding in 3-4 feet biting live bait or jigs under a cork. Big female crappie are in 12-18 feet of water on structures in creek channels. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 10-15 feet of water on jigs.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to good in boat slips and on brush on jigs and shallow on jigs and good reports have been coming from the river.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs and minnows in coves and off of the channels. Bass are good with several 7 plus pound fish caught in 5-10 feet of water in the first drop-off zone with soft plastics. Bedding bass are in 6-8 feet of water. Report by Kurt Dove, Pro Bass Guide.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: The crappie seem to be moving up as well, with many anglers catching fish off piers at the state park and around the bridges.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in 5-12 feet of a water on grass with Texas rigged worms, wacky rig senkos and chatterbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: A lot of bass have moved shallow with some fish bedding around the banks. Some bass are on beds and shallow and others are close to spawning.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good stacked up in the reeds. When the water temperature reaches 80s degree bass will group up offshore.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Deeper fish can be targeted with a 5/8-ounce white bladed Hazy Eye Slabs in conjunction with forward facing sonar.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on shallow bushes in 2-4 feet on spacing flats and areas. Crappie are excellent from the mouth of coves to the back of coves with natural colored jigs. Crappie are spawning in the timber west of the bridge. Look for crappie to be in all stages of the spawn within the next two weeks.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good inside the weeds on plastic crawfish and worms.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are very close to moving shallow to spawn. Largemouth bass are in prespawn mode also. Slabs and swimbaits are good lures to start with.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8.96 pounds are fair off the rocks with bladed jigs around the flats and staging areas and squarebill crankbaits in 2-14 feet. Crappie are fair with catches up to 11 inches on jigs in 8-12 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The bass are spawning and the bite is good. Numbers of bass can be caught around the trees with swimbaits, swimjigs, chatterbaits or with slow presentation flukes or wacky style senkos.

reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair in the weeds on plastics.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Points have been producing quite a few bass bites on dropshots, swimbaits, and Texas rigs.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing Tour

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow to fair with catches under 5 pounds in less than 4 feet of water and in the creek. Bass should be in a prespawn within the next week. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting soft plastics in 2-7 feet of water on timber. Bass are in all stages of the spawn.

reports.text: Largemouth bass are good for numbers using dropshot rigs and crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good as most have bedded up. Crappie have been off and on pushed up shallow one day then out to 24 feet of water the next day.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on the main lake structure with slabs. Crappie are fair in boat slips and on brush on jigs and shallow on jigs.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 25 feet of water on live minnows. Bass are in a post spawn pattern, cast big crankbaits or Texas rig power worms to 8 feet of water.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow later in the day in deeper water with shaky heads and lizards.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Catching small bass shallow with bait fish streamers. The crappie should be moving shallow and Wooly buggers can be a good choice. There are tons of prespawn crappie and some active spawning fish. This week there were numbers of roaming crappie not relating to structure.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be in a prespawn within the next week. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Bass are staging at the mouth of spawning pockets in about 6-8 feet of water. Crappie are good on minnows and jigs with fish moving towards the back of the creeks in about 6 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and some largemouth bass are starting to move towards their spawning grounds especially on those warmer days. Limits of crappie have been reported near standing timber north of the railroad bridge. Largemouth bass are fair to 7 pounds near creek entrances using soft plastics.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Continue to deadstick with a slight sway with a slab on a stinger hook with a 1/16 ounce jighead 3 inch stick bait with a curly tail 2 feet above.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are not cooperating, but some catches in Luces Bayou. Largemouth bass are out in submerged timber and points.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be in a prespawn within the next week. Target bass with Carolina rigs and football head jigs. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good shallow with wacky worms, Texas rigs, and swimbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Look for bass on wind blown points at the mouth of creeks, they are heading to spawning areas. Bank anglers will start to see bass cruising along in protected areas. Crappie will be shallow also in shallow timber areas.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are spawning in 1-5 feet of water. Black bass are in the creek systems, guarding nests, and in the back of the coves along with the crappie. Target bass are good early morning in 1-5 feet of water casting a white and chartreuse spinnerbaits to the bank then reel it slowly back to the boat. The rest of the day target bass from the bank to 7 feet around submerged button willows or shallow timber with a Texas rig, darker color worms, or senko.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: The crappie pattern is consistent with fish in all stages of the spawn. Crappie are good in 3-12 feet with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Many bass are on or around beds with this first wave of spawn.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair in or near to river channels and on points in 30-58 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 2-30 feet of water on brush piles, submerged timber, and submerged cover close to a drop off ledge. Largemouth bass are staging around spawning pockets in 4-10 feet of water. Crappie are still on deep brush and trees in 20 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass and crappie can be caught in spawning areas and backs of creeks. Crappie 3 feet or less hitting minnows. Largemouth bass are in 4 feet or less on Texas rig and chatterbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on light colored bladed jigs, underspin swimbaits and redbug colored worms. Crappie are good in 10-20 feet of water suspended over brush.
reports.by: Hambone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Female bass are starting to parade just outside the spawning grounds. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent with green pumpkin wacky rigs up shallow, or light Carolina rigs. Crappie are slow while fish are in a transition.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are best in the morning on docks with a slight preference of minnows over jigs. No reports on bass.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to 6 pounds in the back of pockets and some creeks. Crappie are slow.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are hit-and-miss in shallow water, and in 10-15 feet of water on structure. Some female bass can be caught on shallow beds with rattle traps and soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass and black bass can be caught while targeting crappie. Crappie are good on minnows and jigs in shallow water.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Look for big bait balls in 22-34 feet of water with 3/4 ounce slabs with 2 jigs tied 16 inches apart. Small roadrunner type baits and small crappie jigs working. Crappie are fair on minnow with fish relating to brush 18-24 feet deep moving on and off structure and starting to roam the deep flats.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass, hybrid striper and crappie are up the creeks for the annual spawn. Fish are scattered in 25-35 feet of water on points with slabs and jigs. Just a few early spring reports of crappie being caught on minnows in shallow water on both the Richland and Chambers Creek tributaries.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are on beds in some pockets. Bass can be caught flipping into brush and trees with rattle traps. Crappie are moving shallow to set up on beds.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the Marina the crappie bite is good, bluegill are fair on crickets or worms, the catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. On the lake crappie are fair on jigs and minnows over brush in 10-20 feet of water. Black bass are fair on crankbaits and spinnerbaits in 4-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on minnows and jigs off the bottom near docks and on concrete structure. Bass are slow on crankbaits and spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: The white, three-quarter ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab will excel for this application. Largemouth bass continue to move shallower with the spring warm-up.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving towards brush and rocks in the muddy creeks and coves. Bass will become more active as the water temperature creep into the 60s.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with many fish in 1-6 feet of water biting senkos, wacky worms and Texas rigged lizards.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to good in shallow water on minnows and jigs. Bass are in 5-6 feet of water and in 12 feet of water. Bass are in pre-spawn pattern. With the third full moon behind us the bass are getting ready to make and get on beds. Good bass caught all the way up the submerged grass on the edge of the water but are not quite on beds yet. The Crappie bite is good, and fish are being caught from 15 feet in the creek channels all the way into the grass depending on which area of the lake you are fishing. Minnows on slip floats are outperforming jigs for crappie.
reports.by: The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good stacked on brush in 14 feet of water in river channels with chartreuse jigs tipped with minnows. Male crappie are pushing shallow to spawning beds. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Target bass in areas where submerged vegetation remains.
reports.by: Team YAKUSA

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in open water suspended 15 feet down with minnows. There are still a few in the crappie house and in boat slips. Bass are fair pushing shallow to spawning areas.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 30-40 feet of water on jigs and minnows.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Numbers of crappie can be caught off channels. Bass are best early in the morning in shallow water with chatterbaits and crankbaits. Most bass are still in a pre-spawn pattern. Report by Kurt Dove, Pro Bass Guide.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be shallow to spawn. Some reports of crappie catches on bright contrasting colored jigs while water is stained.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in 5-12 feet of water in grass with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senko and chatterbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over brush 25 feet of water. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass continue to be good fishing small profile Alabama rigs and jerkbaits around suspended fish in deep water. The full moon will kick off bass spawning in the shallows and in the creeks.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great in the reeds hitting small profile Texas rigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Fish on the main lake continue to show strong interest in the white 5/8 ounce, Bladed Hazy Eye Slab worked by very slowly and steadily reeling the lure up off the bottom using a “slow smoking“ technique.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent from the mouth of coves to the back of coves with natural colored jigs. Crappie are spawning in the timber west of the bridge. Look for crappie to be in all stages of the spawn within the next two weeks.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Soft plastics and slabs will put them in the boat. Crappie are in pre-spawn mode also, females are deeper while the males may be quite a bit shallower. Largemouth bass are moving up too.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 9.23 pounds are fair off the rocks on Hag’s all around jigs in juice box around steep banks and squarebill crankbaits in 2-14 feet of water. Crappie are fair to 1 pound on jigs and minnows off points in brush piles 15-20 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is about to be on fire with the warm spring forecast.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to spawn with many catches with minnows and worms. Bass are good.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow to fair with catches under 5 pounds in less than 4 feet of water and in the creek. Bass should be in a pre-spawn within the next week. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The water level has come down, so the bass bite has shifted from reeds to dead timber. Bass are biting soft plastics in 2-7 feet of water. Bass are in all stages of the spawn.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek continues to boast numbers of largemouth and channel catfish in this power plant lake. Largemouth bass are good on dropshots rigs and crankbaits near creek channels.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are plentiful in shallow water with rattle traps, chatterbaits, swimbaits and soft plastics. Crappie are a bit fickle on and off in 12-22 feet of water.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in 2-10 feet of water focussing on timber in the river channels with crappie jigs. Look for crappie to be in all stages of the spawn within the next two weeks.
reports.by: River Bottom Boys Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on main lake structures with slabs. Crappie are fair in boat slips and on brush on jigs and shallow on jigs.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Catching small bass shallow with baitfish streamers. The crappie should be moving shallow and Wooly buggers can be a good choice. There are tons of prespawn crappie and some active spawning fish. This week there were numbers of roaming crappie not relating to structure.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be in a pre-spawn within the next week. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving towards the back of the creek and coves. Bass are feeding early and late on shad imitation baits. Good on slabs and spoons.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are best on those warmer days when they are more active. Soft plastics and slow rolling crankbaits are putting those largemouth bass in the boat. Crappies are still holding on deeper structure but are sure to start moving towards their spawning grounds.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 6 pounds on jigs and worms fished near heavy timber. Crappie are good on slip bobber rigs fished in shallow water.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Continue to deadstick with a slight sway with a slab on a stinger hook with a 1/16 ounce jig head 3 inch stick bait with a curly tail 2 feet above.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: If you are chasing largemouth bass, small grubs and crawls seem to entice great bites. Crappie are good in Luces Bayou on brush piles anywhere from 8-14 feet of water with small jigs with shad imitations.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Target bass with Carolina rigs and rattle traps. Crappie can be caught with jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be in a pre-spawn within the next week. Target bass with Carolina rigs and football head jigs. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great skipping baits under every dock, or working around the edges with moving baits like crankbaits or spinnerbaits in shad colors.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water on soft plastics Texas rigged, wacky rigged, or dropshots.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are on the move due to the current warming trend. Small bass can be found shallow, and the bigger bass are right behind. Crappie are becoming more active.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Most of the crappie are scattered in 10-20 feet on brush piles, submerged timber. Crappie should be pushing shallow as the weather warms. Slabs and 3-4 inch flukes have been catching sandies. Expect to catch a couple black bass in your journey to the black water. Black bass can be caught in 1-5 feet of water on rocks or concrete with a white and chartreuse spinnerbait with a half of a zoom motor oil worm as the trailer. Texas rig and bass jigs are pulling bass out of 15-20 foot deep brush piles. Crickets have been king as they also catch a few crappies.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie pattern is consistent with males on spawning nests waiting for the females. Crappie are good in 3-12 feet with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass fishing is about to take-off. Many bass are on or around beds with this first wave of spawn.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass and crappie can be caught in spawning areas and backs of creeks. Crappie 3 feet or less hitting minnows. Largemouth bass are in 4 feet or less on Texas rigs and chatterbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good over the hydrilla using bladed jigs and swimbaits, spinnerbaits and redbug worms. Crappie are good fishing brush and laydowns in 15-25 feet with minnows and pintail jigs.
reports.by: Hambone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent in 3-5 feet of water on stick baits and bladed jigs. Crappie are excellent roaming in large groups on brush piles in 5-10 feet of water with chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with a few 5 pounds possible on Alabama rigs and large glide baits. Rip a chatterbait through the top of grass to land the bass prestaging there. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent with green pumpkin wacky rigs up shallow, or light Carolina rigs. Crappie are slow while fish are in a transition.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. It is also important to slow down your retrieve this time of year to trigger these lethargic pre-spawn largemouth. Crappie are fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are best in the morning with a slight preference of minnows over jigs.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to 7.5 pounds. Bass are starting to move shallow in some areas. Some schooling bass in deeper pockets as well biting small minnows or shaky heads. Crappie are slow in the mouth of The Colorado River near Yellow Bluff.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The black bass bite has been improving in shallow water. The crappie are still slow, but hopefully will start improving soon.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite has slowed after the recent rain pushed fish back to deeper water. When the weather warms crappie are ready to spawn with fish full of eggs. Bass like that are slow.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on small swimbaits and wacky rigs in 5-8 feet of water. Crappie are slow on live minnows.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Both species are scattered in 35-40 feet of water on points in the main lake hitting slabs and jigs. A few early spring reports of crappie being caught on minnows in shallow water on both the Richland and Chambers Creek tributaries.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow to move on spawning beds while water is coming in, and water is being released. Bass are in the creeks, points and pockets staging in near spawning areas in 8 feet of water. Crappie are moving to creek pockets, and catfish are transitioning to creek pockets to spawn.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville marina the crappie bite is fair, bluegill are fair on crickets and worms, and catfish are fair on minnows and punch bait. On the lake crappie are fair on jigs and minnow over brush 10-20 feet of water. Black bass are fair on craw jigs and diving crankbaits in 4-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: Black bass bite is still fair.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on minnows and jigs. Bass are slow on crankbaits and spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: When fish are found, utilize a slow steady retrieve off the bottom with a white 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab. Largemouth bass fishing is beginning to improve with more fish moving shallower into less than 12 feet with each warming day this week.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on jigs in shallow water. Largemouth are slow, but there is light at the end of the tunnel as the forecast shows warm temperatures for the next 10 days.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing will pick up with the rain and inflow in creeks and coves. Bass are moving up and becoming more active with the rise in water temperatures and levels.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Lots of bass on the bank spawning or in prespawn. Crappie are picking back up in the backs of the creeks with roadrunners and tube jigs. Bends in the creeks have been the best place to hold the bigger crappie in 6-8 feet near shallow flats.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in shallow water or in brush.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can be caught as shallow as 2 feet with jigs or minnows. Bass are staging in drains and areas leading to spawning flats weightless plastics, crankbaits, and spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Holton Walker, Holton Walker Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in the creeks with jigs tipped with minnows on brush piles in 16 feet of water. Crappie are in a prespawn in the deep creek channels. Male crappie will move shallow to beds in the next two weeks with the warmer weather in forecast. Catfish can be caught as by catch targeting crappie. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.
reports.by: Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair moving out of the crappie house to the shallows to spawning beds. Crappie are being caught with eggs, and fish are starting to move shallow staging for the spawn. Bass and catfish are slow deep and around rocks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are beginning to move up the rivers in shallow water in preparation for spawning. White bass are fair on slabs in 20-30 feet of water. Largemouth bass are fair using soft plastics on deep structure.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in shallow water in the river and in creeks.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair over brush in 20-30 feet of water on jigs. Crappie will move shallow to spawning locations as the water continues to warm.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good under trees and brush on jigs. Prespawn activity is high for crappie and bass full of eggs. The most consistent bass bite is in 20 feet of water dragging plastics. Bass are slow on Alabama rigs and football jigs near deep water. Report by Kurt Dove, Pro Bass Guide.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: The bass are starting to pull up shallow to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good fishing small profile Alabama rigs and jerkbaits around suspended fish in deep water. The full moon will kick off bass spawning in the shallows and in the creeks.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great in the reeds hitting Texas rigs. Bass are spawning on the intake side, but the spawn is finished on the discharge side.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Look for small male bass around sandy banks in mouths of coves. Small streamers and craw patterns should produce bass. Crappie and catfish should be moving shallow when the weather stabilizes, wooly buggers should work well.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting to stage in 1-4 feet of water in spawning areas behind timber and backs of pockets with grass flats.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: It is possible to fish at the crappie house.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are being caught in side weeds on plastics.
reports.by: Harry Lamb, Alamo Texas Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. Hybrids and sand bass are fair on soft plastics and slabs. Largemouth bass are also in prespawn mode.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 5 pounds are fair on minnows off the rocks, Hag’s All around jigs in juice box around steep banks, and squarebill crankbaits in 2-14 feet of water. Crappie are fair to 1 pound on jigs and minnows off points in brush piles 15-20 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are shallow with wacky and Texas rigs, while a shaky head, Carolina rig and crank bait should work well for offshore structure fish.
reports.by: the Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 2-15 feet with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: We need a long stretch of nights in the upper 50s or low 60s to really turn the bass on.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with a shaky head or a dropshot around rocks and outside grass lines, or working a chatterbait over top of the grass.
reports.by: Evan Coleman, Big Bassin Fishing Tour

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite is on docks and in creeks with minnows or jigs.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be staging to spawn off the bank with soft plastics.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Reports of good largemouth bass catches with soft plastics.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: High winds stirring the water clarity, so expect crappie and bass to be scattered. Target bass with Carolina rigs and football head jigs. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 2-5 feet of water near the reeds and stumps with soft plastics and a few bites on swimbaits. Bass are in all stages of the spawn.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek continues to boast numbers of largemouth bass and channel catfish. Largemouth bass are good on crankbaits and soft plastic on many areas of the lake.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good in 1-8 feet of water on rattle traps, and plastics. Crappie bite has been on and off due to the fronts, but good overall in 2-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Bradley Doyle, Bradley Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling up under bait, and can be caught with Alabama rigs, spinnerbaits, spoons, and underspins.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on main lake structure with slabs and in mid depths on chartreuse and white artificial minnows. Crappie are fair in open water roaming patterns and in mid depths and main lake structure on jigs. Crappie should be gearing up to spawn within the next week.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good for numbers but not size. Bass are in all stages of the spawn.
reports.by: Mark Fransen, Fransen’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass have made a big move to the shallows with some on beds in 1-3 feet. Catching small bass shallow with bait fish streamers. The crappie should be moving shallow and Wooly buggers can be a good choice. The Lake Fork crappie bite is really good, if you can stand the cold weather and beat the winds. If you find a crappie and hold an artificial bait above it still enough most fish are crushing that bait.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: High winds stirring the water clarity, so expect crappie and bass to be scattered. Target bass with Carolina rigs and football head jigs. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting early and late in 15 feet of water on brush with minows and jigs. Bass are slow. Good on slabs and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in numbers moving from the deep to shallows on those warmer days. Crappie are holding near deeper structure but are sure to start moving shallow with the warming weather. Best bait for crappies includes small jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on jigs and black Power Worms. Crappie are good up river at night on minnows and good in shallow water on slip bobber rigs.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: There are a few back lakes that are stained and that seems to be the ticket as far as largemouth bass goes. With the water level rising the largemouth bass should transition back to cypress trees. Crappie are great in Luces Bayou eating small jigs in 8 feet of water, but should move back shallow to spawn by the weekend.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: High winds stirring the water clarity, so expect crappie and bass to be scattered. Target bass with Carolina rigs and football head jigs. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught near the bank on soft plastics. The buck bass seem to be moving shallower.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting mid range in 6-10 feet of water on soft plastic creature baits. Crappie can be found on bridge pickings and deep wood on minnows.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass are schooling up under bait, and can be caught with Alabama rigs, spinnerbaits, spoons, and underspins. Some bass are related to grass hitting shad and bluegill colored bladed jigs.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 10-20 feet of water on brush piles and deep submerged timber. Crappie are hugging the bottom so you have to let a ⅛ ounce hand tied jig touch the bottom and then slowly lift to entice a bite. Black bass are in 1-5 feet on rocks or concrete, and in 5-10 feet of water shoreline structure. Texas rigs and bass jigs are pulling them out of 15-20 feet deep brush piles. The dam has trees and brush bluegill and crappie are mixed in. Crickets have been king as they also catch a few crappies.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 3-12 feet with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are slow to fair on deep flats and in river channels in 42-64 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 2-30 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 3 feet or less biting minnows. Prespawn crappie are staging in 10 feet of water on brush and standing timber leading to bedding areas. Largemouth are in 5 feet or less near docks, stumps and bedding areas hitting Texas rigs and chatterbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good over the hydrilla using bladed jigs and swim baits. Crappie are fair to good finding brush in 12-15 feet with minnows and power bait champ minnow on �¼ ounce jig heads.
reports.by: Hambone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in shallow grass with a bladed jig, lipless crankbait or june bug weightless worm. Crappie are fair chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Despite a beautiful week of weather bass fishing was tough with a few catches over 5 pounds with a squarebill crankbait and the Alabama rig. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are fair in shallow water with a weightless worm. Crappie are slow in shallow water.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases in 1-3 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Crappie were fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie limits on the north end of the lakes near creeks with jigs. White bass are making an appearance in the evenings while fishing for crappie.
reports.by: Navarro Mills Marina

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Reports of a few crappie in the mouth of creeks and main rivers in 8-12 feet suspended around trees.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass bite has been slow. Crappie bite is improving on small jigs, with the size of the fish being caught is improving as well.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass and crappie should move off the bank to staging areas post frontal pattern. Crappie may be caught in 8-16 feet of water. Bass can be caught on soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to bite along the bank on minnows and jigs. The crappie spawn will begin any day. Sand bass and hybrids are being caught by anglers targeting crappie. Black bass are slow.
reports.by: Lake Palo Pinto RV Park

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent in shallow water on a fluke or weightless worms. Crappie are fair on live minnows.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Look for big bait balls in 20-34 feet of water with 3/4 ounce slabs with 2 jigs tied 16 inches apart. Small roadrunner type baits and small crappie jigs working. Crappie are fair on minnow with fish relating to brush 18-28 feet deep moving on and off structure and starting to roam the deep flats.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Male bass are in the hay grass, or on the outside of the buckbrush. Bass are staging on points and stumps hitting Carolina rigs or rattle traps. Crappie are moving up the creeks to spawn.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: High winds stirring the water clarity, so expect crappie and bass to be scattered. Crappie are slow on minnows and jigs. Bass are slow on crankbaits and spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: We have been seeing good numbers of these fish fishing different creeks and rivers above the lake on crappie jigs. Crappie are good in 2-5 feet on jigs when we have a warm up. Bass have been slow, but anticipate the largemouth bass bite to turn on in the next 10 days.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Look near creeks with the water flow and rising water temperature for crappie. Bass fishing will improve as water temperatures rise.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair in 1-5 feet of water with wacky worms, senkos and Texas rigged lizards. Some bass can be caught on main and secondary points with shallow crankbaits and Carolina rigs. Crappie improved to good until this last blast of cold air slowed the bite.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be hit-or-miss.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
