reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting to bed in some places though it is still very early.
reports.by: Team YAKUSA

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to good in the Crappie House on jigs and minnows. Crappie are being caught with eggs, and fish are starting to move shallow staging for the spawn. Bass and catfish are slow deep and around rocks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 12 feet of water on minnows and jigs.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are beginning to move up the rivers in shallow water in preparation for spawn. White bass are fair on slabs in 20-30 feet of water. Largemouth bass are fair using soft plastics on deep structure.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on the main lake structure with slabs. Crappie are fair to good on brush piles and in the river on jigs. Crappie should be gearing up to spawn within the next week.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow, but should be staging to spawn. Crappie are staged on brush in 8-12 feet getting ready to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie good on minnows in 18-28 feet of water.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on main and secondary points 10-20 feet with deep water access close by.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are shallow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been consistently shallow for the last couple of weeks. Fish along the bank early in the morning with moving bait has been good for catches of bass.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good on watermelon seed flukes and watermelon red pearls around thin reeds. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop. Bass are holding along and in the cane and reed patches.
reports.by: Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Bass and crappie are spawning shallow. Bass are hitting Texas rigs, jigs, spinnerbaits and wacky rigs. Crappie are biting minnows and jigs. Report by Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding.
reports.by: Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair scattered in 2-20 feet of water biting minnows or jigs. Sand bass are excellent under the Texas State Highway 21 bridge hitting white or chartreuse slabs or minnows. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are on spawning beds. Bass are good in shallow water out to 12 feet of water using weightless skinny dippers, chatterbaits, and lipless crankbaits. Black bass are starting to spawn in the backs of creeks and coves with roving males in the shallows, streamers, and crawfish patterns are excellent for these fish. Look for crappie around brush and retaining walls shallow, small wooly buggers are excellent.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with catches up to 7 pounds along the rocks with chatterbaits and senkos. Crappie are good in the marina or around hardwood main lake or creek entrance.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are shallow in the north end. Largemouth bass are looking for spawning areas. Slabs and deadsticking are catching fish.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are excellent with catches up to 8.30 pounds on jerkbaits, chatterbaits, topwaters and crankbaits in 3-8 feet of water. Bass are in a pre-spawn mid lake, and starting to get on beds on the lower end. Crappie are excellent, suspended in 10-12 feet of water on brush piles in the cove pocket on black and chartreuse jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass were suspended on brush piles hitting jigs. Consistent fishing patterns for catfish, crappie and bass near the restaurant, off rocks and floating docks with small minnows, worms, and cut bait.
reports.by: The Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are spawning, stay in 2 feet or less with a fluke, senko, lizard or swimbait and cover water around trees and pad stems.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Slowly retrieve shiny slabs or spinnerbaits off the bottom to catch these fish in depths of 17-26 feet of water. The crappie have also migrated back into the main lake.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good off the docks with many undersized catches. Largemouth bass are good.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are being caught in numbers with catches up to 8 pounds on soft plastics and crankbaits.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass seem to be on spawning beds. Crappie have been a big hit-or-miss, some anglers are having success with post spawn fish in 10-17 feet of water using a minnow or a 1/32 ounce jig.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been slow due to the fluctuating weather patterns. Bass have moved up and are nesting, small crawfish patterns will work well. Crappie are shallow, small fish patterns like wooly buggers are a good bet. Crappie fishing has been up and down and all over the place this past week.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good hitting 7 inch curly tailed or straight worms, spinnerbaits and crankbaits in less than 10 feet of water. Crappie are in a pre-spawn. Report by Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding.
reports.by: Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and bass are moving shallow to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass action has been good from Indian Harbor to in town on slabs jigged off the bottom in 10-20 feet of water. Crappie action is improving in the creeks and sloughs, but many are still being caught on the main lake structure on jigs from Water’s Edge to the Peninsula. Granbury largemouth bass are fair to good to 6 pounds on soft plastics and spinnerbaits near bedding areas. Some good largemouth bass continue to be caught near major creek entrances.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on various baits fished up river. Crappie are fair in shallow water on slip bobber rigs.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Best catches are being caught on larger profile slabs with larger hooks. Reports that black bass are good.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to transition to structure in 8-14 feet of water, and will be on bulkheads and in the shallows when the shad spawn begins. Crappie can be caught with hand tied jigs and plastics. Largemouth are being caught early in the morning and later in the evening in the backwaters of the lake on plastics and starting to blow up a bit in frogs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: The second wave of spawning largemouth bass and crappie should begin soon. Largemouth bass are spawning on beds. Largemouth bass are good in 1-7 feet of water with wacky worms, weightless Texas rigs, yum dingers or swim jigs. Crappie are in 10 feet or less using minnows on standing timber, brush, or deep docks.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are still in a post-spawn in 5-10 feet of water hitting crankbaits, shaky heads spinnerbaits and Carolina rigs. Crappie are up the creeks on minnows or jigs. Report by Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding.
reports.by: Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting good from the bank to 14 feet with soft plastics, and topwaters.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Big bass are biting shallow and in full spawn mode. Crappie are anywhere you like to catch them.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good within 2-6 feet of water biting on minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing. Most bass are in 10 feet or less. Bass are good shallow on weightless skinny dippers, chatterbaits, and lipless crankbaits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: The second wave of spawning largemouth bass and crappie should begin soon. Largemouth bass are good on spawning beds in 1-4 feet of water in the creek channels using swim jigs, Texas rigs, spinnerbaits, and chatterbaits. Crappie are good fishing minnows in brush, standing timber, and creek channels in 1-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good fishing in the hydrilla with senkos, wacky rigged worms and swimbaits, or shaky heads on red worms off points and deep brush will work too. Crappie are good using minnows over brush in 15-25 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with primarily male bass schooling offshore, but females will start to join post spawn. Offshore bass are hitting crankbaits and Carolina rigs. Crappie are fair in the grass with a beetle spin or rooster tail, any small jig.
reports.by: Wyatt Frankens, Wyatt Frankens Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on red chatterbaits flipping soft plastics in the reeds in 1-3 feet of water. Look for spawning bass shallow. Crappie are good around boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around the dam.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with many limits being caught.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Look for fish in 2-20 feet of water with live shad, small slabs and jigs.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent fishing jigs over grass in the lake, and with minnows suspended over brush piles and off the Prairie Branch fishing pier. Crappie spawn is in the early stages. Bass are excellent, anglers are reporting great catches on topwater frogs early in the morning.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in the grass lines in 4-20 feet of water biting soft plastics and spin baits. Crappie are slow. The bite bass bite has been fantastic!
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Catfish, crappie, and bluegill are fair on minnows, worms, and stink bait at Somerville Marina early morning. Black bass are fair in 3-6 feet of water hitting spinnerbaits, and crankbaits. Crappie are fair on the main lake brush piles in 14 feet of water and pilings biting minnows and very small jigs.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs using electronics to fish brush in the little mineral arm 15-22 feet of water. Smallmouth or largemouth bass are slow fishing docks and structure with crankbaits and spinnerbaits.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Lots of bass are still spawning in 1-5 feet of water hitting wacky-worms and senkos. There are good numbers of bass starting to show up that have already spawned, these fish spawned on that February full moon. With the next moon coming, there will be more bass on the move towards the back. Crappie are good, but with the colder weather will delay it several days. The crappie are super picky due to the changing weather.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: White bass are excellent running up the rivers hitting small chartreuse slabs. Largemouth bass are good out to 5 feet of water using senkos, Texas rigs, spinnerbaits and crankbaits. Crappie are fair, a few weeks from moving shallow to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on Alabama rigs, jerkbaits and weedless swimbaits over the grass. Despite the full moon, only a few bass were on beds this last week, so expect the spawn this next week.
reports.by: David Report by David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are biting at the crappie house and the marina near rocks. Bass are starting to transition to shallower water for the pre-spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on main lake points and drains with deep water access are holding spawning fish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is good at the dam and around the bridges on black and chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are on spawning beds in 2-4 feet of water. Some bass are staging in 4-8 feet on grass lines and breaks hitting shad patterned jerkbaits and chatterbaits over the top of grass. Crappie are fair and scattered in 2-8 feet of water fishing a minnow under a float. Crappie should start to spawn soon.
reports.by: Jim Brack, Athens Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been consistently shallow for the last couple of weeks. Bass are good with catches up to 4 pounds in the grass lines from Quinlan Park north using soft plastic worms.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake B.A. Steinhagen fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass should be transitioning to shallow water hitting soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good working the reeds and grass with weightless swimbaits and flukes. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop. Bass are holding along and in the cane and reed patches.
reports.by: Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Now that the water has cooled and the fish have vacated shallow water, the larger �¾ ounce white Bladed Hazy Eye Slab has been working.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be shallow looking for beds. Crappie should be running the creeks getting ready to spawn. Report by Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding.
reports.by: Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair scattered in 2-20 feet of water biting minnows or jigs. Sand bass are excellent under the Texas State Highway 21 bridge hitting white or chartreuse slabs or minnows. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are on spawning beds. Bass are good in shallow water out to 12 feet of water using weightless skinny dippers, chatterbaits, and lipless crankbaits. Black bass are starting to spawn in the backs of creeks and coves with roving males in the shallows, streamers, and craw patterns are excellent for these fish. The bass will be moving shallow and deeper as the weather changes. Look for crappie around brush and retaining walls shallow, small wooly buggers…
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are very close to being on spawning beds. Crappie are close to spawning as well.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 7.61 pounds are good on jerkbaits, chatterbaits, topwaters and crankbaits in 3-8 feet of water. Bass are in a prespawn mid lake and starting to get on beds lower end. Crappie are fair on brush piles on minnows in 10-12 feet with some in 1-4 feet starting to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass bite is strong flipping cattails and dragging hard bottom. Consistent fishing patterns for catfish, crappie and bass near the restaurant, off rocks and floating docks with small minnows, worms, and cut bait.
reports.by: The Aggie Anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be good in 2-12 feet of water on chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are starting to spawn and if in the right area, many catches can be had flipping trees in 2-5 feet of water.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite continues to be good with fish moving in the shallows around trees, the grass and pad stems in the flats.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Retrieve shiny slabs or spinnerbaits off the bottom at a very slow retrieve to catch these fish in depths of 17-26 feet of water. The crappie bite has picked up in the creeks and inlets in 2-10 feet of water throughout the entire lake. We are now seeing the crappie migrate back into the main lake.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good from the bank out to 10 feet of water using soft plastics, or spinnerbaits. Crappie are good in shallow water with live minnows, or black and chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Channel catfish and crappie are biting real good in 10-20 feet of water. Reports of a lot of small sized largemouth bass. Crappie are good in 15-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs at the docks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek black bass action continues to be good working soft plastics worms and centipedes near spawning beds.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth seem to be moving on up. Plenty of buck bass in shallow water, but some pretty decent ladies have been caught as well. Some crappie have been caught lately but not in good numbers. Hybrids are in 8-24 feet of water in the creek channels and shallows hitting swimbaits, live bait or jigging slabs.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 2-6 feet of water around boat houses with minnows or jigs. Sand bass are good on main lake points in 10-20 feet of water with yellow or chartreuse slabs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are good in shallow water out to 12 feet of water using weightless skinny dippers, chatterbaits, and lipless crankbaits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on main lake structures using slabs. Crappie are fair in boat slips and on brush on jigs and shallow on jigs.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Lake Fork bass bite has slowed down a bit with dropping water temperatures. Bass are moving up and down with the weather changes, I’m offering shallow and subsurface until I find a working pattern. Small craw patterns will work well on bedding bass. Crappies are moving to the creeks and staging, small fish patterns like wooly buggers are a good bet. Crappie fishing has been up and down and all over the place this past week.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Reports of crappie catches continue to be good in the intake using jigs or minnows. Largemouth bass are good on soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie catches are still best on submerged structures, but many are being caught in the river near Tin Top as well. Largemouth bass are slow to fair to 7 pounds on spinnerbaits and shallow diving crankbaits near main lake points and creek entrances.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on red shad power worms, white spinnerbaits, and crankbaits fished in shallow water up river and in Willis Creek. Crappie are fair on slip bobber rigs fished in shallow water.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Many catches are undersized, so use larger profile slabs and larger hooks. Reports that black bass are good.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hawkins fishing report
reports.text: Look for bedding bass in the grass and shallow brush.
reports.by: Guide Alex Guthrie, Fly Fish Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to show up in numbers and getting up on structure on 8-14 feet of water being caught on minnows and hand tied jigs in the silver and black and chartreuse color. Largemouth bass are shallow on structure and scattered. Bass are being caught on worms, cranks and grubs.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is good shallow or deep on soft plastics, chatterbaits, and swimbaits. More bass are pushing to the banks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with in 2-6 feet of water biting on minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing. Most bass are in 10 feet or less. Bass are good shallow on weightless skinny dippers, chatterbaits, and lipless crankbaits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappies are showing up in the shallows in 2-4 feet of water. Seeing some pre-spawn black bass males in 3-5 feet of water using 3-6 foot divers with Texas rig worms and creature baits.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 4-12 feet of water with orange and chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Lake LBJ has been on fire as of late with bass catches up to and over 10 pounds.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Some sandies are up the creeks as well biting slabs, jigs, and live bait. Crappie are fair to good in the main lake and creeks in 5-32 feet of water on bridge columns, brush piles, rock piles, stumps, and laydowns with minnows and jigs. Crappie are slow on live minnows and jigs. Largemouth bass are starting to transition to pre-spawn areas in 5 feet of water. Bass are good flipping jigs, spinnerbaits or any soft plastics.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on senkos and wacky rigged worms fishing the hydrilla, or Texas rigged worms on deep brush. Crappie are good using minnows over brush in 15-25 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Couple of nice largemouths and of course the walleye. Bass are fair to good on minnows and artificials. Crappie are fair on artificial baits and minnows. White bass are good on minnows, slabs, or any vertical presentations.
reports.by: Kenneth Wysong, SharKens Honey Hole

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Male bass are on beds, the females are still staging on points preparing to move shallow. The crappie are spawning in heavy cover.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is good on jigs and minnows in 1-15 feet of water. Bass fishing is good in 2-8 feet of water on plastics around structure and baits that displace water on grass lines and edges of structure.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: After the recent rains the water temperature cooled pushing the crappie to deeper water and slowing the bite.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair to good in 2-20 feet of water with live shad, small slabs, and jigs in white or silver.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Reports of decent size catfish and crappie catches near the dam. Largemouth bass can be caught on soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on artificial worms. Crappie are good on crappie bites, crappie rigs, and minnows. Bluegills are excellent on hot dogs, crappie bites, and worms at the docks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good as the fish stage to spawn on mid flats mid lake 24-30 feet water and are relating to bottom more than suspended using slab jig combo. Crappie are fair in shallow water 1-3 feet by the reeds and golf-coarse and are moving in and out of shallow water for spawning.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Catching the white bass a little shallower than before in 35-40 feet of water using slabs.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass and hybrid stripers are fair to good fishing with slabs, sassy shad and live bait off the 309 flats and main lake points in 20-30 feet of water. Crappie can be caught in shallow water coves and creek channels with minnows.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in the grass lines in 4-15 feet of water biting soft plastics and spin baits. Crappie are transitioning to the pockets to spawn. The bite bass bite has been fantastic!
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: The black bass bite is starting to improve with some fish being caught in the 3-4 pound range.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing is improving as new hydrilla begins to grow and the lake warms toward preferred spawning temperatures bringing many fish up shallow.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Swimbaits have been the ticket for the bigger fish and slabs for the white bass. Crappie are spawning right now. The largemouth bite is good on docks and riprap with crankbaits, hogs and worms are all catching them in 1-4 feet.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in the creeks in 1-5 feet of water using jigs and minnows on brush sticking up or lay downs from the bank. Largemouth and smallmouth bass are fair on swimbaits along the bluffs and on sandy points with stumps in 5-8 feet of water.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Lots of bass are still spawning in 1-5 feet of water hitting wacky-worms and senkos. There are good numbers of bass starting to show up that have already spawn, these fish spawned on that February full moon. With the next moon coming, there will be more bass on the move towards the back. Crappie are good, but with the colder weather, it is going to pop it back several days. The crappie are super picky due to the changing weather.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in 10 feet of water crankbaits and spinnerbaits, and trick worms. Crappie are scattered and the bite is slow on minnows and jigs.
reports.by: Paul Taylor, The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: White bass are excellent in the river on small chartreuse slabs, and fly anglers are having success with clousers or live minnows. Largemouth bass are good out to 5 feet of water using senkos, Texas rigs, spinnerbaits and crankbaits. Crappie are fair, a few weeks from moving shallow to spawn. Largemouth and crappie should be spawning by the coming full moon.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are great with catches up to 9.7 pounds on soft plastic worms.
reports.by: David Report by David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Smaller sized crappie are biting at the crappie house. Bass are starting to transition to shallower water for the pre-spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie good on jigs and minnows over structure in 18-35 feet of water.
reports.by: The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on main lake points and drains in 10-20 feet of water casting swimbaits, jigs, rattletraps, crankbaits, wacky rigged worms and senkos.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arrowhead fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to move in and out.
reports.by: Brandon Brown, Brown’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Quite a few bass are shallow with a handful of fish on beds.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good on green pumpkin creature baits in the shallows near the reeds. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop. Bass are holding along and in the cane and reed patches.
reports.by: Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be up shallow looking for beds. Crappie should be running the creeks getting ready to spawn. Report by Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding.
reports.by: Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding

reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair with fish in 5-10 feet of water biting minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are good in shallow water out to 12 feet of water using weightless skinny dippers, chatterbaits, and lipless crankbaits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 12.49 pounds are good on jerkbaits, chatterbaits and crankbaits in 3-8 feet. Bass are in a prespawn and starting to get on beds. Crappie are fair using minnows on brush piles in 6-10 feet and starting to move shallow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 2-12 feet of water on chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are starting to spawn and if in the right area, many catches can be had flipping trees in 2-5 feet of water.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Target bass in the trees with flukes and senkos in dark colors this time of year.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Use small weighted jigs with a small plastic tail to get these fish to bite or try using a double or triple tandem bait or a silver slab spoon to try different depths. The crappie bite has picked up in the creeks and inlets in 2-10 ft of water throughout the entire lake. We are now seeing the crappie migrate back into the main lake.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good in 8 feet or less using soft plastics, swimbaits, and spinnerbaits. Crappie are good in shallow water with live minnows, or black and chartreuse crappie jigs.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Channel catfish and crappie are biting real good in 10-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good to 6-7 pounds on spinnerbaits and soft plastics fished near stickups near creek channels.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth seem to be moving on up. Plenty of buck bass in shallow water, but some pretty decent ladies have been caught as well. reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Corpus Christi Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 5 feet of water on jugs and live minnows.
reports.by: Captain Damian Hubbs, Top Gun Outfitters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good fishing around boat houses with minnows or jigs. Sand bass are good on main lake points in 20-30 feet of water with white or chartreuse slabs. reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on main lake structure on slabs, and some are being caught staging near creeks on rooster tails and inline spinners. Crappie are fair in boat slips and on brush on jigs and shallow on jigs.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Bass are spawning in waves with some fish being caught in 3-5 feet of water flipping bushes along vertical hardwoods with a hard bottom, and in the backs of creek in 1-5 feet of water. Crappie are fair using a slip bobber with a jig at the backs of creeks in visible timber.
reports.by: Ram Reyes, Ram Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are loaded up ready for the spawn at the backs of pockets and creeks.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with lots of fish in the shallows, and some are spawning. Bass are in the shallows working streamers are working in 1-8 feet. Crappie will be moving towards the banks, small patterns like wooly buggers are a good bet. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork has been really good this past week.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Reports of crappie catches continue to be good in the intake using jigs or minnows. Largemouth bass are good with reports of big fish over 13 pounds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs and minnows, with some moving shallow. The bridges are crowded indicating the crappie are heading to the creeks. Bass are improving as fish become more active, and some smaller bass are moving shallow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Black bass, crappie and sand bass continue to be reported as fair to good on the upper ends of Granbury near the Farm-to-Market 51 bridge and near Tin Top. Many of the largemouth bass and crappies are moving towards the back of sloughs especially on those warmer afternoons. Striped bass have been slow with sporadic catches reported from Decordova to the dam using slabs and live bait.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good in shallow water on various baits fished up river. Crappie have been slow this week with some caught up river suspended 6 feet down.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Spotlock with the trolling motor and thumper in 26-32 feet of water with any color and size of slab, but the bigger the slab the better to hook larger sandies. Reports that black bass are good.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are hitting crankbaits, worms and grubs. Crappie are starting to pick up on structure in 8-16 feet of water on small jigs, silver and black and chartreuse are good.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass seem to be everywhere, on the bank, and mid level depths.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: With the warm water and temperatures the bass are on the move heading to the spawning areas. Bass will stage on the first depth break, timber line, or structure very close by. Crappie are being found in the rivers or creeks on the trees or brush, some are shallow. It’s definitely crappie time, so grab your favorite jigs or minnows and go fishing.
reports.by: Gilbert Miller, GTB Outdoors

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with some fish showing up shallow in 2-6 feet of water biting on minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing. Most bass are in 10 feet or less. Bass are good shallow on weightless skinny dippers, chatterbaits, and lipless crankbaits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 3-15 feet of water with some fish setting up on spawning beds. Seeing some pre-spawn black bass males in 3-5 feet of water using 3-6 foot divers with Texas rig worms and creature baits.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 2-15 feet of water with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Lake LBJ has been on fire as of late with bass catches up to and over 10 pounds.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Some sandies are up the creeks as well biting slabs, jigs, and live bait. Crappie are fair to good in the main lake and creeks in 5-32 feet of water on bridge columns, brush piles, rock piles, stumps, and laydowns with minnows and jigs. Early mornings are the best for white bass, crappie, and largemouth bass. Crappie and white bass can be caught on small flutter spoons, roadrunners, small shad style swimbaits. Largemouth bass are near secondary points halfway back in the creeks best water temperature upper 50s degrees using spinnerbaits, wacky rigged senkos and squarebill crankbaits in 5-10 feet of water. Bass should move shallower.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good along the hydrilla and main lake points with darker colored wacky rigged worms, and swimbaits. Crappie numbers are increasing.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with bass schooling offshore, and some shallow getting ready to spawn. Offshore bass are hitting crankbaits and Carolina rigs. Crappie are fair in the grass with a beetle spin or rooster tail, any small jig.
reports.by: Wyatt Frankens, Wyatt Frankens Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Always remember that many Naconiche bass bed deeper than most other East Texas lakes. Do not forget that bluegill are the enemy for bed protecting bass. Crappie population is good.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair on red chatterbaits and flipping soft plastics in the reeds in 1-3 feet of water. Crappie are good around boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around the dam.
reports.by: the Angelo State Fishing Team

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on black and chartreuse jigs in 1-3 feet deep creeks.
reports.by: Clay Major, Major Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is good on jigs and minnows in 1-15 feet of water. Bass fishing is good in 2-8 feet of water on plastics around structure and baits that displace water on grass lines and edges of structure. Most small crappie jigs and minnows will catch them.
reports.by: Sam Parker, Freshwater Fishing Adventures

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in shallow water on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair to good using small slabs and small jigs, but some can be caught using small live bait also.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on artificial worms. There was an angler report of a 9 pound bass caught on a chatterbait this week. Crappie are good on crappie bites, crappie rigs, and minnows. Bluegills are excellent on hot dogs, crappie bites, and worms at our docks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: White bass are excellent and have grouped up in large schools staging for spawning on deep flats mid lake 24-30 feet water and are relating to bottom more than suspended using slab jig combo. Crappie are slow on deep brush piles and trees roaming in deep water.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: White bass are in the creeks but can still be caught out on the main lake 45-55 feet on points and humps subtly jigging any flashy slab.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass and hybrid stripers are fair to good with fish being caught on a slab and jig combination off Pelican Island and main lake points in 25-30 feet of water. Reports of crappie being caught in the shallow water in coves and creek channels on minnow.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are trying to spawn deeper than normal in 4-12 feet of water. Bass are hitting jigs, crankbaits and Texas rigs. Crappie are good on minnows and jigs in the creeks. Large groups of bass are making the push shallow in 3-15 feet in the grass and hydrilla. Bass are hitting Texas rig stick bait, lightweight Carolina rig, rattletrap, and chatterbait.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Catfish, crappie, and bluegill are fair on minnows, worms, and stink bait at Somerville Marina early morning. Black bass are good in 3-6 feet of water hitting spinnerbaits, and crankbaits. Crappie are fair on the main lake brush piles in 14 feet of water and pilings biting minnows and very small jigs.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow casting into shallow water in the coves. Crappie are slow to fair at the crappie house and in the shallow water but should improve as the water temperature warms.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: After that, ferret out groups of bottom-oriented fish holding in tight groups and fishing them vertically with a white, 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab has been producing in 21-31 feet.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Swimbaits and slabs have been the ticket in 30 feet. The crappie bite has been very sporadic. The largemouth bite has been good on riprap and shallow cover including dock pilings and isolated stumps are holding fish.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing is good in the creeks and on shallow brush in warmer and dirtier water. Bass are fair on white swimbaits along the bluffs in the backs of the coves and on gravel banks.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: The bass are spawning with most of fish in 1-5 feet of water. The Crappie bite is good in the creeks in 3-8 feet of water using jigs, roadrunners and minnows.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are loaded up ready for the spawn at the backs of pockets and creeks.
reports.by: Bryan Cotter, Texas Hawgs

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in the river channel in 8 feet of water suspended as shallow as 2 feet deep.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with some big fish being caught in the grass lines in 3-8 feet of water with finesse baits. Some bass are beds but most will begin spawning within the next two weeks.
reports.by: David Report by David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are pushing shallow with some still biting minnows and jigs in the crappie house. Bass are slow with a few shallow on beds hitting spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be fair on small jigs and minnows fished near deeper structure. Largemouth bass continue to be fair along structures and docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in the river and in creeks, river and shallow.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting the yearly spawn. Bass are good on main lake points, main lake flats, and drains near the river channel and deep water creeks in 5-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Raul Cordero, Far West Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is really good. Bass have moved shallow on cover with the best baits on crankbaits, creature baits, jigs on shallow cover.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are pushing shallow for the spawn. Crappie are fair and scattered moving shallow minnow under a float in shallow water 2-6 feet of water. Crappie should start to spawn soon. Crappie are susceptible to changes in weather, so expect the fish to move deep after a drop in temperature.
reports.by: Jim Brack, Athens Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are shallow, preparing to spawn with some fish on beds right now.
reports.by: Carson Conklin, ATX Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been good on green pumpkin creature baits in the shallows near the reeds. Report by Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop. Bass continue to be good working soft plastics like 4 inch worms, flukes and craws in or on the edge of grass lines.
reports.by: Jason Hernandez, Bass Institute of Bastrop

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Fish found in open water between 20-42 feet deep can be drawn in with thumping, seen on Garmin LiveScope, and caught with a vertical retrieve using white, 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving up the creeks gearing up to spawn, the cold spell pushed them back some. Bass pushed back to deeper water biting crankbaits, jigs and spinnerbaits. Report by Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding.
reports.by: Camron Wilkerson, Camron’s Quality Crappie Guiding

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair with fish scattered 2-20 feet of week throughout the lake with minnows or jigs. Sand bass are good with fish stacked under the Texas State Highway 21 bridge with yellow or white slabs in 20-30 feet of water. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are good in shallow water out to 12 feet of water using weightless skinny dippers, chatterbaits, and lipless crankbaits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Spring seems to be coming early this year so the bass are moving up earlier. Crappie will be shallow and looking to spawn as well.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are very near their spawning time. Crappie should be on northern docks with minnow and jigs. Crappie are not up on the banks just yet.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass catches to 5.75 pounds are good on Hag’s Bait jigs, jerkbaits and crankbaits in 3-8 feet of water. Bass are in a prespawn in the mouth of cove pockets. Crappie are fair on brush piles using minnows in 6-10 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Catfish, crappie and bass can be caught near the restaurant, off rocks and floating docks with small minnows, worms, and cut bait. Bass are good shallow but can be caught on brush piles during the day.
reports.by: The Bait Barn

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 2-12 feet of water on chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Travis Holland, TH Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The bass spawn is on so the bite should be on fire, but the lake level is falling so this bite can slow until the water stabilizes.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 10-15 feet of water biting on minnows. Lots of bass activity chasing bait out to 15 feet deep.
reports.by: Lake Cisco Rentals

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek black bass fishing continues to be good on soft plastics.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Smaller buck bass are shallow making beds, so the big girls should not be far behind. There are a few crappie up shallow, but not enough to write home about.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair with fish scattered 2-20 feet of water, with some fish pushing shallow using minnows or jigs. Sand bass are good on main lake points with slabs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing. Bass are good in shallow water out to 12 feet of water using weightless skinny dippers, chatterbaits, and lipless crankbaits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good on main lake structure on slabs. Crappie are fair to good in boat slips and on brush on jigs and some crappie are being reported shallow on jigs.
reports.by: Chad Ferguson of North Texas Catfish Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are active on a variety of baits after this warm spell. Bass are in the shallows working streamers are working in 1-8 feet. Crappie will be moving towards the banks, small patterns like wooly buggers are a good bet. The crappie fishing on Lake Fork has been really good this past week.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be good on small jigs amd minnows fished near deeper structure like bridge pilings. Largemouth bass continue to be good in numbers on soft plastics fished in the river above Granbury and near main lake points.
reports.by: Michael Acosta, Unfair Advantage Charters

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good on red shad PowerPoint Worms and black jigs. Crappie are good on slip bobber rigs fished in the backs of coves and sloughs all over the lake.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: White bass are 22-32 feet of water on the bottom biting slabs on stinger hooks using a thumper.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are scattered in the bottom in 8-16 feet of water on structure being caught on hand tied jigs and small plastics. Largemouth are being caught early and later around docks and rip rap.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are spawning on beds. Largemouth bass are good in 1-7 feet of water with wacky worms, weightless Texas rigs, yum dingers or swim jigs. Crappie are in 10 feet or less using minnows on standing timber, brush, or deep docks.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent in the main creek channel north of the Texas State Highway 155 bridge with minnows or jigs. Report by Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing. Most bass are in 10 feet or less. Bass are good shallow on weightless skinny dippers, chatterbaits, and lipless crankbaits.
reports.by: Marty Thomas, Lake O’ the Pines Crappie Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 2-15 feet of water with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Slabs, jigs, and live bait are working. Crappie are fair to good in 5-32 feet of water on bridge columns, brush piles, rock piles, stumps, and laydowns. Crappie are being caught both in the main lake and in the creeks. Early mornings are the best for white bass, crappie, and largemouth bass. Crappie and white bass can be caught on small flutter spoons, roadrunners, small shad style swimbaits. Largemouth bass are near secondary points halfway back in the creeks best water temperature upper 50s degrees using spinnerbaits, wacky rigged senkos and squarebill crankbaits in 5-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Wes Campbell, BendARod Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are spawning on beds. Crappie are good fishing minnows in brush, standing timber, and creek channels in 1-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: White bass are spawning in the Betsy Creek, White Rock Creek, Harmon and the Trinity River using Duck Tracker slabs. Crappie and largemouth bass are in the shallows spawning in 1-4 feet of water along grassy shore lines. Target crappie with crappie jigs, for bass throw chatterbaits, creature baits on beds, or topwater frogs cast in the grass.
reports.by: Michael Richardson, Lake Livingston Adventures

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on topwaters early, red bug colored worm Texas rigged and wacky rigged along hydrilla. Crappie are fair to good in brush piles from 15-25 feet of water using shad colored jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: The buck bass have not moved shallow in mass yet, but it should be very soon. Always remember that many Naconiche bass bed deeper than most other East Texas lakes. Crappie population is good.
reports.by: Eric Wolfe, NacoTack Fishing Services

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 2-5 feet of water on spinnerbaits and chatterbaits. Crappie are scattered but starting to move shallow biting crappie minnows or jigs.
reports.by: Wendell Ramsey, Ramsey Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are being caught using Alabama Rigs and small swimbaits. Bass are moving shallow.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to spawn, but half finished. Target crappie in 1-14 feet of water with jigs and minnows. Largemouth bass are good in 2-8 feet on baits that make a lot of commotion such as chatterbaits.
reports.by: Sam Parker, Freshwater Fishing Adventures

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in brush piles biting on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting Texas rigs, chatterbaits and wacky rig stick baits.
reports.by: Captain Hank Harrison, Double H Precision Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are fair to good in 2-10 feet of water with small slabs and small jigs are the way to go, but some can be caught using small live bait also. Stripers to 17 pounds are good on slabs and 5 inch swimbaits from Broadway to Costello Island. White bass are excellent on slabs near Bone Bend, Peanut Patch and in the back of Cedar Creek.
reports.by: TJ Ranft, Ranft Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass bite are improving for bank anglers using a purple pinkish colored soft plastic Texas rigged. Bank anglers are reporting a good bite for crappie and catfish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Anglers are reporting good catches of bass and crappie around the entire lake. Bass are biting at our Colony fishing pier, an angler recently caught a 5-pound bass on live worms. With the improving visibility, anglers can target bass with live worms, artificial worms, and on topwater frog lures early in the morning. Crappie are biting on crappie jigs, crappie bites, and live minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: White bass are excellent and have grouped up in large schools staging for spawning on deep flats mid lake in 24-30 feet water relating to bottom more than suspended using slab jig combo. Crappie are slow on deep brush piles and trees roaming in deep water, jigs or minnows keeping the baits not far off bottom.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: White bass have been good in the main lake in 45-55 feet of water on slabs. Many reports of crappie and white bass catches in the creeks.
reports.by: Justin Wilson, Wilson Outdoor Connection

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Large groups of bass are making the push shallow in 3-15 feet in the grass and hydrilla. Bass are hitting Texas rig stick bait, lightweight Carolina rig, rattletrap, and chatterbait. Expect bass to stay in the grass lines casting dark colored senkos and plastics so the fish can see the lure. Crappie and the catfish are in the back pockets and creeks to spawn.
reports.by: Captain Hank Harrison, Double H Precision Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: Catfish and crappie fair and bluegill slow on minnows, worms, and stink bait at Somerville Marina early morning. Black bass are fair, hitting spinnerbaits, jerkbaits and crankbaits. Crappie are fair on the main lake brush piles and pilings in 14 feet of water on pilings, but the best bite is up creeks, now full of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow to fair as fish transition shallow. Bass are fair, with small bass in the coves. Bass are still not on beds but some can be found staging on rocky points. Crappie are good near concrete and in the crappie house.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Fish found in open water between 22-30 feet deep can be drawn in with thumping, seen on Garmin LiveScope, and caught with a vertical retrieve using white, ⅝ ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slabs.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow around the boathouses and on brush piles in 12-15 feet of water. Largemouth and smallmouth bass are fair on plastics down the bluffs as the sm begin to bed around the gravel flats and in backs of coves. Largemouth are still on stumps in 5-10 feet of water on swimbaits.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Guaranteed Guide Service Lake Texoma

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is good from 2-18 feet of water. Lots of bass spawning, so the best baits are wacky-worm and Carolina rigs with lizards and brush hogs. Crappie are starting to show up in numbers from the creeks to the main lake docks biting jigs and minnows.
reports.by: Stephen Johnston, Johnston Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 8-12 feet of water in the rivers and creeks on jigs or live minnows. Crappie should spawn within the next few weeks.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 4-16 feet of water in the creek beds with minnows and jigs. Crappie are spawning shallow for the next few weeks. Bass are in 10-12 feet of water using crankbaits, and black trick worms, spinnerbaits and crankbaits.
reports.by: Paul Taylor, The Boulders at Lake Tyler

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 8-13 feet of water on lake Waco, with good numbers being caught in the creeks and rivers.
reports.by: Zach Minnix, Jig N’ Jerk Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Walter E. Long fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 10 feet of water or less with chatterbaits and swimbaits early and late, switching to finesse baits throughout the day. Bass are strong using worms in green colors with red or blue flakes, Alabama rig and spinnerbaits. Crankbaits are catching some good largemouth and hybrid stripers. Crappie are starting to pile up as well. A small crappie jig with a chartreuse head and light colors is working well for those. Crappie are fair in 20 feet of water using chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: David Report by David Townsend, Austin Fishing Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Weatherford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in the crappie house with minnows and jigs. Bass continue to be slow, with a few catches in 15-20 feet of water using Texas rigs and crankbaits. Expect the bass to push shallow soon for the spawn.
